claims.feature: other: surface polish with nothing underneath
claims.claim: Mollick calls such posts meaning-shaped attention vampires that take mental effort to decode and give no equivalent understanding in return.
claims.source: Ethan Mollick, Wharton professor, One Useful Thing, 26 May 2026

claims.claim: Mollick writes in a footnote that AI is notoriously weak while seeming strong at fiction writing, and that ChatGPT in particular is fond of meaningless similes and metaphors.
claims.source: Ethan Mollick, Wharton professor, One Useful Thing, 26 May 2026
claims.quote: fond of meaningless similes and metaphors

claims.claim: Mollick argues that such similes can feel profound at first sight only because readers assume difficult writing is purposeful and work hard to assign it meaning.
claims.source: Ethan Mollick, Wharton professor, One Useful Thing, 26 May 2026

claims.claim: Mollick states that a little bit of effort can make AI writing less cliche, more personal, and more worth using in moderation.
claims.source: Ethan Mollick, Wharton professor, One Useful Thing, 26 May 2026
claims.quote: a little bit of effort can make AI writing less cliche
claims.page: paragraph beginning "This is not a condemnation"

claims.claim: Mollick states parenthetically that frequent AI users have historically done quite well at identifying AI writing.
claims.source: Ethan Mollick, Wharton professor, One Useful Thing, 26 May 2026
claims.quote: frequent AI users have historically done quite well identifying AI writing

claims.claim: Goodspeed locates the failure of AI imagery not in the technology but in the cliche and superficial creative ambitions of the people using it.
claims.source: Elizabeth Goodspeed, It's Nice That columnist, in her column reproduced on ABC Brand/Design
claims.quote: AI image generation is essentially a truncated exercise in taste

claims.claim: Kirk et al. measured that RLHF fine-tuning reduces output diversity relative to supervised fine-tuning across their range of diversity metrics.
claims.source: Kirk, Mediratta, Nalmpantis, Luketina, Hambro, Grefenstette and Raileanu (UCL/Meta/Oxford), ICLR 2024
claims.quote: RLHF significantly reduces output diversity compared to

claims.claim: Kirk et al. found that raising the RLHF KL penalty coefficient produced a drop in per-input diversity rather than the expected gain.
claims.source: Kirk, Mediratta, Nalmpantis, Luketina, Hambro, Grefenstette and Raileanu (UCL/Meta/Oxford), ICLR 2024
claims.quote: drop in per-input diversity, rather than a gain
claims.page: Section 6.3, The Impact of the KL Penalty

claims.claim: Kirk et al. state it is unclear whether the generalisation-versus-diversity tradeoff is fundamental to RLHF fine-tuning or a deficiency of current methods.
claims.source: Kirk, Mediratta, Nalmpantis, Luketina, Hambro, Grefenstette and Raileanu (UCL/Meta/Oxford), ICLR 2024
claims.quote: It is unclear whether this tradeoff is a fundamental one in fine-tuning

claims.claim: Kirk et al. restricted their diversity evaluation to the summarisation task.
claims.source: Kirk, Mediratta, Nalmpantis, Luketina, Hambro, Grefenstette and Raileanu (UCL/Meta/Oxford), ICLR 2024
claims.quote: For the diversity evaluations, we focus on the summarisation task specifically

claims.claim: Kirk et al. report seeing no meaningful diversity differences among their instruction-following models.
claims.source: Kirk, Mediratta, Nalmpantis, Luketina, Hambro, Grefenstette and Raileanu (UCL/Meta/Oxford), ICLR 2024
claims.quote: we did not see any meaningful differences

claims.claim: At 6.7 billion parameters Kirk et al. report a per-input EAD diversity score of 0.07 for the RLHF model against 0.79 for the SFT model.
claims.source: Kirk, Mediratta, Nalmpantis, Luketina, Hambro, Grefenstette and Raileanu (UCL/Meta/Oxford), ICLR 2024

claims.claim: Zhang et al. report that Verbalized Sampling, a training-free prompting strategy, increases creative-writing diversity by 1.6 to 2.1 times over direct prompting.
claims.source: Zhang, Yu, Chong, Sicilia, Tomz, Manning and Shi (Northeastern/Stanford/WVU), arXiv 2510.01171 v4

claims.claim: Zhang et al. conclude that mode collapse can be mitigated at inference time.
claims.source: Zhang, Yu, Chong, Sicilia, Tomz, Manning and Shi (Northeastern/Stanford/WVU), arXiv 2510.01171 v4
claims.quote: mode collapse can be mitigated at inference time

claims.claim: Zhang et al. state that aligned models retain significant inherent diversity.
claims.source: Zhang, Yu, Chong, Sicilia, Tomz, Manning and Shi (Northeastern/Stanford/WVU), arXiv 2510.01171 v4
claims.quote: aligned models retain significant inherent diversity
